audit.why: Lane-bully-into-scaler shape is right: he owns 1-3 and his 6, Vladimir stabilizes at 4-5 and wins from two items as Pantheon falls off. Packet flags the chart as contradicting the 54.4% owner WR (Pantheon gets 5/7 stages), but the stage story — Vlad wins by scaling, not by stages — is coherent; noted for the user rather than changed, since the kits cannot adjudicate stage ownership.

audit.whatIsWrong: Full-layer chart disagreed with content/packet on four rows: phases[3] said Pantheon (content: Vladimir), phases[4-6] said Skill (content: Pantheon, Pantheon, Vladimir).
audit.why: Content win[] matches the packet exactly, so full sides move alone with rewritten whys per the chart rule.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[0].text labeled Shield Vault as (E) — Shield Vault is his W (600-range dash stun, 13-9s); Aegis Assault is E (frontal invulnerability, 22-18s). Two bleed bullets and no digit in cooldowns. suspectName 'Use Grand Starfall' is a false positive — the name is correct inside the sentence.
audit.why: Kit slots: Q Comet Spear 11-8s, W Shield Vault 13-9s stun dash with auto-reset (missingInteractions: the reset wind-up is the pool cue), E Aegis Assault 22-18s, R Grand Starfall 180/165/150s. The auto-reset tell was unstated anywhere.
audit.corrected: Slot letters fixed, cooldown numbers inserted, bleed bullets rewritten (one now carries the auto-reset pool cue).

edits.before: - Pantheon Shield Vault (Stun): matchup-defining — Point-and-click stun — respect the all-in any time it is up. Check it before every step-up. - W Sanguine Pool is the lifeline; chip damage never gets it. - The ult answers fights, not waves.
edits.after: - Shield Vault (Stun) cycles every 13-9s — a dash stun; respect the all-in any time it is up and check it before every step-up. - Comet Spear pokes on an 11-8s loop. - W Sanguine Pool is the lifeline; chip never gets it. The ult answers fights, not waves.

edits.before: Q the last-hit, E-charge as he steps to answer, release and walk — the trade costs him HP and pays yours.
edits.after: His W stun opens with an auto-reset wind-up — that is your pool cue; the 2s puddle outlasts his burst window.

edits.before: Pooling his poke and then eating the real engage at half HP with nothing — the pool is a combo-breaker, not a flinch reflex.
edits.after: Charging E inside his 600-range Shield Vault reach hands him a free stun combo — always build the charge a step outside it.

edits.before: The crimson rush timing — Q empowers every third-ish cast and the sustain war starts tilting your way.
edits.after: Your Tides of Blood sustain now outheals his poke — the crimson rush stabilizes and tilts levels 4-5.

edits.before: Hemoplague online — the all-in inverts: Q-E-R-E with ignite kills most mids who thought they were winning.
edits.after: His 6 beats yours — Grand Starfall adds roam and dive pressure and his stun all-in still outruns your heal.

edits.before: Riftmaker timing: every trade heals more than it costs. Extended fights are now donations to your health bar.
edits.after: Still his until the item actually lands — a committed W-E-Q all-in outpaces your heal before Riftmaker completes.

edits.before: Late Vlad is a raid boss: pool their engage, R their clump, and drain whatever stayed to argue.
edits.after: Late Vlad is a raid boss — pool his engage, R the clump, and drain whatever stayed to argue.

edits.before: Your empowered Tides of Blood plus Transfusion lets you shove and heal, but respect Pantheon's Comet Spear (Q) poke and his point-blank Shield Vault (E) all-in that shrugs your first Q back.

notes: Packet defect worth surfacing to the user: the level chart gives Pantheon 5 of 7 stages while Vladimir wins 54.39% of 1993 games — the chart may over-credit his level-6 and first-item rows, but the kits cannot settle stage ownership so I aligned the full layer to the existing content chart rather than re-adjudicating. suspectName 'Use Grand Starfall' confirmed as a false positive (correct name inside a sentence) — no edit. spikes[2]'s claim that pool dodges 'his committed E' is plausible (Aegis strikes are dodgeable while untargetable) but not kit-verifiable; left alone.
